findings.claim: Declared inclusion rule versus practiced set. Declared (lane-policy.md:71-73): "The protected set includes every exclusive dispatch lever and suite/conformance gate entrypoint named here as exact paths: `ops/bin/dispatch.sh`, `ops/bin/go.sh`, `ops/bin/suites.sh` and `ops/conductor/tools/laneconf.py`." Practiced (ops/bin/dispatch.sh:2-6): "dispatch.sh — the lever's front door. The wrapper itself lives with the instruments at ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh ... exec bash ...". The protected path is a six-line shim; the 326-line lever body `ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh` — which resolves `LAUNCHER_PIN` (line 107) and sets `WF_AGENT` for the launcher (line 245) — is tracked, sits inside `dev`'s only write root `ops/`, and is absent from `protected_authority_paths`, with `dev.authority_maintenance: false`. A routine `dev` job therefore rewrites the exclusive dispatch lever with no maintenance evidence, while N7 (:425) still passes because it exercises only the shim address. Same asymmetry the other way at `ops/bin/ladder.sh:5`, an unprotected shim onto the protected `ops/conductor/tools/ladder.py`. This is the F1 gap Grok 8cdf11 named, closed at the address and open at the body. Minimal correction: add `"ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh"` and `"ops/bin/ladder.sh"` to `protected_authority_paths`, and extend N7 to name the body path; or, if the four-path list is to stay verbatim, narrow :71-73 to claim only the named addresses and declare the shim/body gap explicitly rather than "every exclusive dispatch lever". `ops/bin/go.sh` and `ops/bin/suites.sh` are real bodies and need no change.
findings.reproduce: git ls-files ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh; grep -n 'conductor/tools/dispatch.sh' ops/lane-policy.json; cat ops/bin/dispatch.sh ops/bin/ladder.sh; grep -n 'LAUNCHER_PIN\|WF_AGENT' ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh; sed -n '71,76p;425p' ops/conductor/lane-policy.md

findings.claim: Admission and standing-grant rotation is unspecified, so the fixture cannot be written. :119-121 binds the custody anchor to the "current admission id"; :165 freezes `standing_grants` as "the complete standing-grant set for this admission" inside immutable ratify-time evidence; :173 routes revocation through the existing supersede transition; :177-178 says a listed row that is missing or invalid "is not an empty set that licenses a per-job fallback", and :171-172 refuses `lane-policy` on missing rows. Together: adding or revoking any standing grant requires a fresh ratified admission, and until it exists a single superseded listed row refuses all protected maintenance. That is fail-closed and probably intended, but no rule states how the anchor's "current admission id" is updated or who checks the replacement, and no P/N row prescribes either outcome (P4:417 exercises one standing record across two jobs; N9:427 covers superseded rows only as forged/invalid evidence). Minimal correction: one sentence that a changed standing-grant set requires a fresh ratified admission plus an anchor update verified by the previously trusted reader, and one case row pairing revoked-standing-row -> `lane-policy` with a post-rotation pass.

Declared: "Notes do not grant or revoke authority" (:174). Practiced in the same contract: "Re-read live at every acceptance transition; an event note changes this digest too" (:139), with N9 (:427) refusing `lane-policy` on a "changed output byte digest (including changed events/newline)". `decisions.py note` requires only `WF_AGENT` identity and host store access (decisions.py:330-334, main:406) — no owner principal — so a note on a bound admission or grant row voids every already-bound dispatch at its next transition, which is withdrawal of acceptance in effect even though the grant is unchanged. :140 bounds the blast radius (a fresh dispatch rebinds the new digest without a new owner act), but the reader must assemble that from three separated sentences and no case row states it. Minimal correction: reword :174 to "notes confer and remove no grant; a note does change the bound digest, so bound dispatches must rebind", and add the bounded consequence to N9 or R2 so the test author knows in-flight refuses and fresh binds.
